posts.name: DerpTheBugbear
posts.cooked:
Well, as funny as it is to name it "punishment" via an anagram... If we REALLY have to decode an hour long morse code video,then I dunno if I'll be participating in this particular puzzle. 

It makes me not really wanna deal with it...  Kinda has the opposite effect that an ARG should have on people... Y'know? Maybe it's just that naming it "punishment" carries a bit too much spitefulness? Or maybe it's a combination of that AND the fact that it's an hour long video as opposed to the last video?  I dunno...  I'm just not feelin' it this time. 

 

Now it would have been funny if you had the punishment anagram, and a new morse code video that was almost exactly the same, but with one or two digits being different in the end result.  People who missed out on decoding the previous video will then be able to if they want to.  And the people who already did it when the old video was leaked will be thinking "What the heck?! I've already done this! The code sounds almost exactly the same! what's going on?"  Punishment for the ones that already did this, and a fun little puzzle for the rest.

 

But I honestly can't get interested in doing an hour long morse code translation.  Even if it is on a loop or something, there's going to be the need to do the whole thing, in case they hide something in one of the "loops".

 

I think the worst part of thinking of this as a "punishment" is that it may make some people irritated at the ones who jumped ahead.  Because everyone gets punished for those 1 or 2 people.

 

I'll be back for the next puzzle I guess... Hope someone actually finishes it soon, but it'll probably be a few hours in any case.

I've played in and run many puzzle hunts.  As an organizer, this is the point at which I would expect teams to start calling me and saying "we're not having fun anymore."  At that point, there are basically three choices: point them to a clue they've missed, give them a hint outside of the hunt to unstick them, or let them suffer.  Basically no one does the third one.

One possibility is that it's only the first bit that matters, and the rest is just filler.  So it's probably worth decoding at least the first few minutes (enough to get a letter or two out of the deepest level).

I still think there's gotta be something we haven't noticed that clues us into how to solve this without decoding over an hour of morse code (and then doing it recursively twice more), but if not, perhaps we should plead with Tim for a pointer.  I don't want to speak for the group, so I won't make this an actual request-- I'll see if others feel the same way, or if someone finds the missing link.
